criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear headings and readable structure, but figures lack numbers, tables lack captions, typos/grammar issues, bibliography URL-only and Wikipedia source; presentation is adequate not professional.

technical_issues.issue: RAAN 27.33° is said to indicate launch facility location; RAAN is inertial and set by launch time/azimuth, not directly by site.
Statement that very high altitude yields low resolution 'which is also desirable' is contradictory; should be undesirable.
STK access table contains duplicate access 15 and inconsistent access 6 (3 Feb start, 4 Feb stop, 365 s), so statistics are unreliable.
Mt Pleasant Radio Observatory is a radio astronomy facility; no evidence/link budget that it can support TT&C/data downlink.
No STK/PIGI software files included in submission; only screenshots/table.
No hand calculation/derivation for SSO inclination or J2 precession; plot only.
Drag-sail deorbit not quantified (sail area, deorbit time, 25-year rule compliance).
Wikipedia used as source [6]; bibliography is URL-only and [10] malformed.
'constant supply of sunlight' inaccurate for SSO; eclipse periods exist.
No data rate/link budget or ground station contact capacity calculation.
Vega E not operational; reliance on unbuilt vehicle with only brief backup.
600 km altitude not justified by swath/resolution calculation; 250 km reef width vs sensor swath missing.

overall: Comprehensive single-satellite coral-reef mission with STK access analysis and all major elements, but technical inaccuracies, missing software files, unnumbered figures/tables and weak referencing (including Wikipedia) reduce quality. Weighted result is around a mid-credit standard.

feedback.summary: Your coral-reef mission is comprehensive and well structured, with all major design elements and a clear STK access analysis. To reach the next level, tighten technical accuracy, include software files and hand calculations, and improve figure/table numbering and referencing.
next_steps: Add STK/PIGI software files and hand calculations (e.g., SSO inclination/J2 precession, link budget, drag-sail deorbit) to support your design evidence.
Correct technical statements: RAAN is not set directly by launch site; remove 'constant sunlight' for SSO; fix duplicate/inconsistent STK access entries and justify 600 km with swath/resolution.
Replace Wikipedia/URL-only bibliography with proper cited sources, number all figures/tables, and proofread for typos and grammar.

criteria.C1: You clearly define the primary mission, need, single-spacecraft rationale and users (CSIRO, BOM) in the Introduction, meeting all requirements. To reach Accomplished fully, strengthen referencing beyond general web pages and add more specific literature support for the mission need and user requirements.
criteria.C2: Your Mission Design covers launch, orbit, manoeuvres, ground control, communications, duration and EOL with STK screenshots and an access table. To move from Adequate to Accomplished, correct the RAAN explanation, fix the inconsistent access table, include software files and hand calculations (SSO/J2, link budget, drag-sail deorbit), and justify 600 km with swath/resolution.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion draws specific, evidence-based conclusions on launch vehicle, orbit and mission benefit, which is strong. To fully secure Accomplished, make every conclusion traceable to report evidence and avoid generic caveats; explicitly link each conclusion to the design results and limitations you presented.
criteria.C4: You use clear headings and a readable structure, but figures lack numbers, tables lack captions, and there are typos/grammar issues. The bibliography is URL-only and includes Wikipedia. To reach Accomplished, number and caption all figures/tables consistently, proofread carefully, and use properly cited, credible references matching in-text citations.
